title: MotorStorm: Pacific Rift
subtitle: The festival reaches an island

body: MotorStorm: Pacific Rift is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 3 off-road racer, first released in North America on 28 October 2008. The second MotorStorm leaves the original game's desert for an island of forests, water, rock and volcanic terrain. Motorcycles, buggies, trucks and other vehicle classes race together on routes with different surfaces and openings. Their differences give a crowded event its shape: a line that suits a light vehicle may expose it to a much heavier opponent. The island changes both the scenery and the decisions made during a lap.

The player uses boost to gain speed while watching the engine's rising temperature. Keeping it active too long risks destroying the vehicle, so its use becomes a sequence of short judgements rather than a permanent accelerator. Water and hot environments affect that balance, making the surface part of the race's timing. Branching routes allow a smaller machine to take a narrow line while larger vehicles force a way through rougher ground. Choosing where to go matters alongside choosing when to commit to another burst of speed.

Monster trucks join the vehicle selection, able to climb over smaller competitors and break through parts of the environment. Riders on motorcycles and quad bikes face a different version of that physical contest, with less protection when opponents close in. Four-player split-screen brings the mixed field into local multiplayer, while additional event types vary the festival's objectives. The game also allowed music stored on the PlayStation 3 to accompany a race. Its expanded terrain and local racing options developed the festival idea before Apocalypse moved it into a collapsing city.
